facts.statement: The genus Arambourgia was established by Kälin in 1940.
The type species of the genus Arambourgia is Alligator gaudryi.
The type species Alligator gaudryi was originally described by de Stefano in 1905.
Fossils of Arambourgia date to the Late Eocene epoch.
Arambourgia is an extinct genus containing only one species of alligatorine crocodile found in Europe.
facts.quote: Arambourgia is an extinct monotypic genus of alligatorine crocodylian from Europe.

facts.statement: Arambourgia possessed non-serrated teeth and a deep snout, distinguishing it from the flatter snouts of most other alligatorids.
facts.quote: Arambourgia had non-serrated teeth and a deep orienirostral snout, unlike the flatter snouts of most other alligatorids.

facts.statement: Recent studies consistently classify Arambourgia within the subfamily Alligatorinae, though its exact placement remains disputed.
facts.quote: Recent studies have consistently resolved Arambourgia as a member of Alligatorinae, although its relative placement is disputed, as shown by the cladograms below.

facts.statement: Based on its unusual anatomy and karstic fossil settings, Arambourgia gaudryi likely occupied an ecological niche similar to modern juvenile and dwarf crocodilians.
facts.quote: Based on its unusual anatomy and it having been found in karstic settings, A. gaudryi occupied an ecological niche analogous to present-day juvenile and dwarf crocodylians.

facts.statement: The parent group for Arambourgia is the subfamily Alligatorinae.
Arambourgia belongs to the family Alligatoridae.
Arambourgia is classified within the class Reptilia.

rejected.statement: Researchers suggest Arambourgia was likely part of an early dispersal event of alligatorines from North America to Europe during the Eocene.
rejected.quote: Arambourgia was likely to have been part of an early dispersal event of alligatorines from North America to Europe during the Eocene epoch.
